summary: The legacy project contains 21 distinct physics experiences in this group. There are ten 2D labs: a spring-cart energy lab (Ch 0), a Hamiltonian phase-space lab (Ch 13), a particle-crossing stress-energy lab (Ch 11), a Couette/Poiseuille viscous-shear lab (Ch 11), a TOV stellar-structure lab (Ch 17), a Schwarzschild photon redshift/Doppler lab (Ch 17), a cosmological distances lab (Ch 19), a numerical FLRW Euler-vs-RK4 audit lab (Ch 20), a GPS clock-rate slider (Ch 16) and a twin-paradox slider (Ch 3). There are also nine three.js 'Spacetime Lab' scenes: Earth free-fall rain flow, covector level planes, light cone, sphere holonomy (atlas only), tidal cloud, Flamm embedding with a proper-length ruler, gravitational-wave rings, an expansion lattice, and ADM lapse/shift. The physics kernels are the strongest part of the group. They are small, pure, unit-declared functions (exact oscillator, exact collisionless crossings with T^{mu nu}=sum p^mu p^nu/p^0, exact laminar profiles, a TOV RK4 in log-enthalpy, Simpson-integrated FLRW distances, a Killing-energy frequency ratio, PG rain radius). Each has independent numerical checks (RK4 vs trig, finite-difference BVP vs analytic, crossing times solved separately, Lane-Emden limit, analytic dust/de Sitter distances, RK4 convergence ratio). All five model-only checks were re-run and pass on 2026-09-12. check-physics-calculations.mjs is also a standalone finite-difference Riemann/Ricci/Kretschmann checker for arbitrary 4D metrics (Kerr, FLRW with k, pp-wave, ADM). The UIs are clean and theme-aware, with honest model disclosures, reduced-motion handling, offscreen pausing, saved state and no-JS fallbacks. Their weaknesses are instructional rather than numerical. Several 3D scenes are orderly but not yet explanatory, per the author's own aesthetic review: embedding, lapse/shift, the expansion observer, and Earth grid density. Some 2D labs hide the key teaching feature, such as the missing mass-radius family in the star lab and the angular-diameter turnover squashed on an axis forced to at least 50 Gpc. The GPS/twins widgets are bare sliders. All rendering is vanilla JS string-templated SVG or imperative three.js inside a static-site build (scripts/*.mjs emit HTML, web/*.js hydrate). The current app/ SvelteKit reader bundles that runtime rather than re-implementing it. For grbook.ai: port the models and checks nearly verbatim, and rebuild views as Svelte/Threlte components. Keep the scientificContext/narrationSource contract as the tutor interface, and redesign the weaker scenes around a measurement. The GPS and twin widgets live in web/app.js, which the SvelteKit app does not bundle, so in the current app they are inert markup with frozen default values.
lessons_learned: Separate the pure physics model (web/*-model.js, relativity-models.js, scene-models.js) from rendering. This single decision made every lab independently testable in Node, and it is why the kernels can move to grbook.ai verbatim.

Every model shipped with an independent check that does not reuse the formula under test. Examples: RK4 vs the trig solution, a tridiagonal finite-difference BVP vs the Couette/Poiseuille formulas, crossing times solved by brute-force plane intersection, the Newtonian n=1 Lane-Emden radius sqrt(pi/2), and analytic Einstein-de Sitter/de Sitter distances. Keep this standard, and wire these checks into CI for grbook.ai.

Each lab publishes a machine-readable data-scientific-context (model, parameters, readouts, units, assumptions, equations, source) and a data-narration-source sentence regenerated on every state change, plus a gr:visual-change event. That is exactly the interface a GPT-Live voice tutor needs to see and describe a live lab. Make it a typed contract in grbook.ai, and add a command interface so the tutor can set parameters.

Passing geometry/layout tests did not make scenes teach. The author's legacy-scene-aesthetic-review.md concluded that embedding, lapse/shift and expansion are 'orderly without yet being explanatory'. The best experiences (particle crossings, fluid cut, photon waves) are organized around one measurement the learner performs.

Put the main teaching feature on the default screen. The star lab hides the maximum-mass turning point: re-running starProfile gives M_max=0.1637 at rho_c~0.32 (the default already gives 96% of it), the default is 0.2 and the slider runs to 2, but there is no M(rho_c) or M(R) plot. The distances lab plots D_A (peak 1.75 Gpc at z~1.6) on an axis forced to at least 50 Gpc and filled by D_L (46.7 Gpc at z=5), where it looks flat.

Numerics controls (radial step, Euler vs RK4, requested step) are valuable in an 'audit the answer' lab but distracting as primary controls in a physics-discovery lab. Progressive disclosure is needed.

String-templated SVG re-rendered via innerHTML each frame, recomputing the full measurement 5-6 times per draw (particle-flow view, readout, insight, crossing, matrix, source), works at this scale but should become memoized derived state in Svelte.

Honest disclaimers are a strength worth copying. Examples: the embedding height is not time or force, the cone rim is not a boundary, the dye is not molecules, the six-direction gas is not thermal equilibrium, the rain observers fall from rest at infinity, and strain is exaggerated and first order.
Fixed camera envelopes computed over the full parameter range (scenes.js captureBounds) prevented crop and jump when sliders move. Reuse the idea in Threlte.

Model-only and browser checks should stay separate. check-mechanics-experience, check-particle-flow and check-fluid-shear exit after the model assertions when given --models. check-relativity-models and check-physics-calculations are model-only. check-relativity-labs is browser-only: it needs a local static server and a Chrome path, and qa/relativity-labs.log records it failing with a Puppeteer TimeoutError (check-relativity-labs.mjs:31) at the notebook-import step. In grbook.ai, CI should always run the physics checks, with browser checks in a separate job.

A stale qa/relativity-labs.log shows the browser suite once timing out at the notebook-import button. The browser checks depend on a local static server and Chrome path, so they were fragile. Keep model checks separate (--models flag) so CI always runs the physics.

The SvelteKit port silently dropped behaviour. app/scripts/prepare.ts re-exports six web modules, but not web/app.js, so the GPS and twin widgets ship as server-rendered markup with plausible default numbers and no script behind them. The failure is invisible in static screenshots and in any test that checks only rendering. Every interactive in grbook.ai needs a behavioural test: move a control and assert that a readout changes.

Hard-coded chart envelopes tuned to one state hide others. Examples: star axes fixed at x 1.3, y 1; evolution fixed at t 8, A 6; distances forced to at least 50 Gpc. This is the 2D counterpart of the good scenes.js captureBounds idea. In grbook.ai, compute envelopes over the parameter range for each curve, or use small multiples, and add a QA assertion that each plotted series spans a minimum fraction of its axis.

assets.title: Mechanics Lab 01: Watch the energy change places (spring and cart)
assets.teaches: Energy shifts between kinetic and spring potential energy while the total stays fixed. Momentum and force are signed vectors, while energy is a non-negative scalar. At turning points the cart is momentarily at rest while the force is maximal, and at equilibrium all the energy is kinetic.
assets.pedagogy: Prediction-free exploration with a state-aware insight sentence (speeding up / storing energy / turning point / equilibrium). A 'Quarter-cycle' button jumps to canonical states. Setup sliders are hidden in a disclosure and reset the clock to zero, and a 'What is being calculated?' disclosure derives q(t) and T=2 pi sqrt(m/k). This is a Chapter 0 preparation lab for novices.

interaction.what_updates: Cart position and spring zig-zag, momentum and force arrows with labels, displacement bracket, the kinetic/potential stacked energy bar and values, the direction readout, and the insight sentence. It also updates the scientificContext/narrationSource and saves state to localStorage.
interaction.rendering: String-templated inline SVG re-rendered on each animation frame; KaTeX in the disclosure; CSS container queries

assets.physics_model: Exact undamped Hooke oscillator in SI units: q=q0 cos wt + p0/(m w) sin wt, p=p0 cos wt - m w q0 sin wt, w=sqrt(k/m). Validated by an independent 1024-step RK4 integration (tolerance 1e-11), energy conservation over a 3x3x3x3 parameter grid, the return to the initial state after T, central-difference Hamilton equations, and a unit Jacobian determinant (phase-area preservation).

strengths: Exact model with independent RK4 and symplectic checks (scripts/check-mechanics-experience.mjs --models passes, re-run 2026-09-12)
Clear hierarchy in the screenshots: separate rows for p and F arrows, readable energy bar and key in both themes and at 390px
Stops animating offscreen or when the tab is hidden, respects reduced motion, and renders a static SVG plus disclosure without JS
issues: Pre-relativistic content only. It is useful as Ch 0 preparation but carries no GR idea.
The time slider is capped at one period, so the learner cannot watch several cycles or damping (no damping model).
The energy bar uses a single-colour gradient per term; at extremes one term vanishes entirely, which reads as a missing element.
Whole SVG replaced via innerHTML each frame (acceptable at this scale, not idiomatic for Svelte)
quality.evidence: scripts/check-mechanics-experience.mjs (model and browser assertions); qa/mechanics-0-*.png inspected

reuse.notes: Keep mechanics-model.js and the check verbatim, along with the copy, insight rules and derivation disclosure. Rebuild as a Svelte component sharing one oscillator store with the phase-space lab. Optionally add a damping toggle and a 'predict the turning point' prompt. Place it in a prerequisites/refresher track rather than the GR core.

assets.size: 113-line JS view + 21-line model + 64-line CSS + 23-line HTML builder (minified style)

assets.title: Mechanics Lab 02: One cart, two ways to see its motion (phase space)
assets.teaches: The same physical state is one point (q,p) in phase space. Motion follows a constant-Hamiltonian ellipse, and the Hamiltonian flow field gives the direction of the next change. The cart view and the phase view are two descriptions of one state, which sets up the action and Hamiltonian formalism used in the GR action chapter.
assets.pedagogy: Linked dual views: the cart on the track and the dot in phase space, with a trail and four nested energy contours. The deck prompts the learner to pause either view and notice they describe the same state. Its placement in Ch 13 prepares Lagrangian/Hamiltonian ideas before the Einstein-Hilbert action and ADM conjugate momenta.

controls: Mass, stiffness, starting q, starting p (disclosure)
interaction.what_updates: The phase dot and trail update each frame. Contours and the flow field are rebuilt only when setup parameters change (a cached phaseKey). The cart view and energy bar update in sync.
interaction.rendering: Inline SVG with quiver arrows and ellipses; fixed axis scale across parameter changes

assets.physics_model: Same exact oscillator. Hamiltonian H=p^2/2m + kq^2/2, flow (p/m, -kq). Contour semi-axes are sqrt(2H/k) and sqrt(2mH). Phase-area preservation is verified numerically with det of the finite-difference flow Jacobian equal to 1 within 1e-10.

strengths: Genuinely linked representations with the same scale; the trail shows the path covered this cycle
Liouville/area preservation is actually checked, not just asserted
Clean desktop composition in the screenshot (cart left, phase portrait right)
issues: Flow arrows are very faint (opacity 0.25) and the contours at 17% opacity are barely visible in the light theme
Area preservation is verified in the check but never shown to the learner (no evolving blob of initial conditions)
Only the harmonic potential is available; there is no pendulum or Kepler effective potential that would link to geodesic orbits

reuse.notes: Keep the linked cart/phase idea and the model. For grbook.ai, add a draggable cloud of initial conditions to show Liouville area preservation, and an effective-potential mode (Newtonian vs Schwarzschild V_eff) so the same phase portrait carries forward to geodesic orbits and the ISCO.

assets.size: Shares the mechanics files; phaseView ~30 lines

assets.title: Matter Lab 01: What crosses the surface? (stress-energy from particle crossings)
assets.teaches: Each component T^{mu nu} is a measurement. The row chooses where you measure (in the box, or across an x/y/z surface) and the column chooses what is carried (energy or a momentum component). The learner sees that opposing streams with zero mean momentum still give a positive normal momentum flux, which is pressure, while their energy flux cancels. Tilted streams give off-diagonal (shear-like) momentum flux whose sign follows the stream angle. A finite crossing count converges to the ensemble average.
assets.pedagogy: Measurement before matrix: the tensor is shown only in a disclosure after the learner has built entries by counting. A 'latest contribution' line shows sign x carried value for a single crossing. Insight sentences are keyed to preset, row and column, and include the two-minus-signs explanation for pressure. Disclosures cover 'why opposite motion can produce pressure' (with a reflecting-wall analogy), building the tensor with the c factors, and the model, units and counting checks.

controls: Preset: One stream / Balanced motion / Tilted pairs
Where to measure: In the box / Across x / y / z (row)
What is carried: Energy / p_x / p_y / p_z (column)
interaction.what_updates: Orthographic 3D cube with 96 depth-sorted particles colored by normal-velocity sign, short velocity trails, flash on crossing, detector plane and normal arrow. Readouts compare the counted estimate with the all-particle average and show positive/negative crossing counts. The highlighted 4x4 matrix entry, the insight text and the scientificContext update as well.
interaction.rendering: Inline SVG with a hand-rolled orthographic projection and painter's-algorithm depth sort; no WebGL

assets.physics_model: 96 collisionless equal-mass particles in a periodic unit cube, with deterministic hashed initial positions. Units: L, L/c, mc, mc^2; four-momentum p^0=gamma, p^i=gamma v^i. The ensemble tensor is T^{mu nu}=sum_a p^mu p^nu / p^0 (per unit volume). Detector crossings are counted exactly via floor/ceil of the unwrapped coordinate, and the signed sum of carried momentum is divided by area x time. The first index is the direction crossed and the second the quantity carried. Checks: mass shell p.p=-1, symmetry, trace = -96/gamma, isotropic diagonal for balanced, T^{xy}=96 gamma v^2 cos sin for tilted, crossing counts against brute-force plane intersections for 3 presets x 3 speeds x 3 angles x 3 axes x 3 planes, a finite-time error bound, long-time (t=1e4) convergence, and an edge-of-interval negative crossing.

strengths: Best-in-group pedagogy: the stress-energy tensor is built from an operational measurement, with the 'pressure without flow' surprise front and centre (docs/particle-flow-review.md)
Exhaustive independent numerical verification (check-particle-flow.mjs --models passes, re-run 2026-09-12)
Honest about limits: not thermal equilibrium, no collisions/viscosity, no observer change
The latest-crossing line makes the sign bookkeeping concrete
issues: Flat SVG projection with small dots; at 390px the cube is small and the controls make the lab very long (qa/particles-slanted-390-dark.png)
No movable subvolume and no boosted observer. The review lists both as outstanding, and a boost is needed to reach T^{mu nu}=(rho+p)u u + p g.
Units mc^2/L^3 and the 'one stream / across x / p_x' default are abstract for a novice without a guided sequence
particleFlowMeasurements recomputed ~6 times per frame (in the view, readout, insight, crossing, matrix and source)
Neutral (grey, zero normal velocity) particles are not in the legend
quality.evidence: docs/particle-flow-review.md; scripts/check-particle-flow.mjs --models (passes, re-run 2026-09-12); qa/particles-slanted-1440-light.png (tilted pairs, 45 deg, v=0.56c, across x / p_x, t=4 L/c: counted 18.640 vs ensemble 18.169, 79/77 crossings, latest contribution +0.478) and the 390 and stream screenshots inspected

reuse.notes: Keep particle-flow-model.js and check-particle-flow.mjs verbatim, along with the row/column framing, the insight rules and the three disclosures. Rebuild the view as a Threlte/three.js scene with instanced particles, larger crossings and a movable box. Add a guided step sequence (density, then pressure, then shear) and a 'boost the observer' step that Lorentz-transforms the analytic tensor, as the review requires. Add a photon-gas preset for p=rho/3.

assets.size: 57-line view (long lines, ~300 pretty) + 32-line model + 46-line CSS + 24-line builder

assets.title: Matter Lab 02: How one layer pulls another (Couette and plane Poiseuille flow)
assets.teaches: Neighbouring fluid layers exchange momentum through shear. Force per area on the lower fluid (tau_yx = mu du/dy) and x-momentum flux toward +y have opposite signs. Flow speed and shear are different quantities: in Poiseuille flow the centre is fastest but has zero shear. At fixed plate speed, viscosity changes force but not profile; at fixed pressure gradient it changes speed but not shear. This motivates what the perfect-fluid stress-energy tensor leaves out.
assets.pedagogy: One movable 'gold cut' links the flow picture and the velocity profile. Action-reaction arrows act on the upper and lower regions. The insight text directs two controlled comparisons, and the sign derivation is spelled out (momentum entering the lower region downward). Pi_ij = rho v_i v_j + p delta_ij - tau_ij is connected to the Cauchy stress. Disclosures derive both profiles from force balance and state what the animation represents: steady states only, dye as a mean-flow tracer, and gauge pressure.

interaction.what_updates: 90 dye markers with trails advect at the analytic speed. Five velocity arrows, the velocity profile curve and probe dot, the cut line and paired shear arrows (labelled 'Zero shear here' at the centreline), pressure labels, the three readouts, the mode intro and the insight text all update.
interaction.rendering: Inline SVG (flow box plus profile plot), KaTeX derivations

assets.physics_model: Steady incompressible Newtonian laminar flow between plates with H=0.02 m, no slip: u(y)=U y/H + G y(H-y)/(2 mu), G=-dp/dx, tau=mu u', flux=-tau, Q=UH/2+GH^3/(12 mu), dissipation = mu U^2/H + G^2 H^3/(12 mu). Validated by an independent 120-cell tridiagonal finite-difference solve of mu u''+G=0 over both modes x 4 drives x 4 gradients x 3 viscosities. Simpson integration checks volume flow and a work/dissipation balance; the wall velocities, pressure gradient and shear sign reversal are also checked.

strengths: Unusually careful sign conventions (force vs flux vs Cauchy stress) explained in plain language (docs/fluid-shear-review.md)
Independent BVP solve plus an energy-balance check (check-fluid-shear.mjs --models passes, re-run 2026-09-12)
The zero-shear-at-max-speed contrast is a strong misconception buster
issues: Non-relativistic continuum mechanics: tangential to a GR course except as motivation for anisotropic stress and the perfect-fluid idealization
Dye markers and velocity arrows are small and low-contrast in the 1440 light screenshot; the pressure-mode drive arrow is teal while the legend uses blue for velocity
Mobile SVG text is rescaled with 21-24px CSS overrides inside the viewBox, a fragile hack
No transient (startup) flow, by design; a learner may still expect to see flow develop

reuse.notes: Keep the model, the check, the sign-convention text and the cut-based design. Place it as an optional 'beyond perfect fluids' enrichment after the perfect-fluid T^{mu nu}, not on the core path. Rebuild the SVG in Svelte with larger markers and proper responsive text. A later link to relativistic viscous stress (pi^{mu nu}) is optional.

assets.title: Stellar structure lab: Build a star from its centre (TOV integration)
assets.teaches: The learner integrates the TOV equations outward from a regular centre until the pressure vanishes, which defines the surface. They read off R, M and compactness 2M/R, see the normalized pressure, density and enclosed-mass profiles, and check numerical convergence by halving the step.
assets.pedagogy: The hint poses 'is a denser star also a larger star?' against a fixed spatial scale. A Star/Profiles view switch is provided. A readout of the change in R when the step is halved introduces convergence diagnostics. The limitation text warns that a mass-radius point does not establish stability. A notebook textarea and CSV export with a provenance header (OV 1939 DOI) are included.

interaction.what_updates: Star disc radius on a fixed 1.2 reference circle with a density-shaded radial gradient, profile curves, four readouts, a sampled data table and the scientificContext
readouts: Change in R when step is halved
interaction.rendering: Inline SVG (radial gradient disc, line chart with wide and compact variants), KaTeX equations in disclosure

assets.physics_model: G=c=K=1 Gamma=2 polytrope: p=rho0^2, epsilon=rho0+p, log-enthalpy h=ln(1+2 rho0). RK4 in r on (m,h) with dm/dr=4 pi r^2 epsilon and dh/dr=-(m+4 pi r^3 p)/(r(r-2m)). The series start at r0=1e-5 and the surface is a linear zero of h. The integrator throws if r<=2m. Checks: the Newtonian limit (rho_c=1e-6) matches Lane-Emden n=1 R=sqrt(pi/2) and M within 3e-5; mass is monotone and pressure non-increasing; radius differences shrink under refinement. Re-running starProfile (step 0.005, rho_c grid 0.01, reviewer re-run 2026-09-12) shows M peaks at 0.1637 (R=0.762) near rho_c~0.32 and falls to 0.1136 (R=0.490, 2M/R=0.46) at rho_c=2 (the unstable branch). The default rho_c=0.2 gives R=0.8658, M=0.1574, already 96% of M_max.

strengths: Real, correctly formulated TOV solver with a clever enthalpy variable that makes surface detection clean
Independent Newtonian-limit validation (check-relativity-models.mjs passes, re-run 2026-09-12)
Provenance-rich record (units, assumptions, limitation, primary source) exported with the CSV
issues: The key physics, maximum mass and the unstable branch, is invisible: the default rho_c=0.2 (M=0.1574) sits just below the turning point (M_max=0.1637 at rho_c~0.32), and the slider continues to 2 on the unstable branch where mass falls to 0.114, yet there is no M(rho_c) or M-R family plot and no warning when crossing the peak
Dimensionless K=1 units are never converted to km or solar masses, so novices get no sense of neutron-star scale
The radial-step control is a primary control, a numerics distraction in a physics-discovery lab
The star picture is a flat gradient disc with little information beyond R

The chart() code hard-codes the profile axes to x in [0,1.3], y in [0,1] (web/relativity-labs.js chart, id==='star'). A low-density star (R~1.19) nearly fills the width, while the rho_c=2 star (R=0.49) occupies about a third of it. No interior-to-exterior metric is shown
quality.evidence: scripts/check-relativity-models.mjs (passes, re-run 2026-09-12); reviewer node scan of starProfile over rho_c in [0.02,2]; qa/lab-star-1440-plot.png (default readouts R=0.86584, M=0.15736, 2M/R=0.36349, dR on halving -3.9e-5)

reuse.notes: Keep starProfile and its check verbatim, plus the record's units/assumptions/limitation text. Redesign the view around the family: a live M-R and M(rho_c) curve with the current star as a dot, the turning point marked and the stability caveat attached. Offer a 'physical units' toggle (choose K to give km and solar masses). Move step size under 'audit the numerics'. Optionally show g_tt and g_rr through the surface into the Schwarzschild exterior.

assets.title: Light and observers lab: Follow the photon, ask each observer (gravitational redshift + Doppler)
assets.teaches: A radial photon's measured frequency depends on who measures it. The static-observer gravitational factor sqrt(f_e/f_r) combines multiplicatively with local special-relativistic Doppler factors gamma(1 - n beta). A receiver moving toward the light can blueshift enough to overcome gravitational redshift. The locally measured light speed is always c, while the coordinate rate f(r) is not a measured speed.
assets.pedagogy: Two wave strips over equal local-time windows make frequency visible as crest count. Emitter and receiver markers sit on an r/r_s axis. The prediction prompt reads 'Can a Doppler blueshift overcome the gravitational redshift?'. The limitation points to the regular-coordinate horizon lesson for crossing.

interaction.what_updates: The received-wave crest count, radius markers, the frequency-vs-receiving-radius plot (specified observers vs both static) and the four readouts
interaction.rendering: Inline SVG wave strips and line chart

assets.physics_model: Schwarzschild exterior with f=1-r_s/r and E_obs=-p_mu u^mu. nu_r/nu_e = sqrt(f_e/f_r) * gamma_r(1-n beta_r)/(gamma_e(1-n beta_e)), with n=+1 outward. The coordinate travel time is Delta r + ln((r_r-1)/(r_e-1)) in r_s/c units, computed but not displayed. Checks: sqrt(4/7) for 2->8 r_s, reciprocity (product of the forward and reverse ratios = 1), pure Doppler 0.5 at beta=0.6, and rejection of r<=r_s.

strengths: Correct observer-based formulation that cleanly separates gravitational and kinematic factors
The wave-crest picture is an intuitive, novice-friendly representation of frequency
Reciprocity and Doppler checks pass (check-relativity-models.mjs)
issues: Defaults (emitter 2 r_s, receiver 8 r_s, both velocities 0) make the 'Specified receiving observers' and 'Both observers static' curves identical, so the Frequency plot shows one line with a two-entry legend (qa/lab-photon-1440-plot.png: readouts 0.75593 = sqrt(4/7), motion factor 1)
Only 4 cycles are drawn, so small ratio changes are hard to see; there is no photon worldline or spacetime diagram
The coordinate travel time is computed but never shown, a missed chance to contrast coordinate and local speed
Velocities are 'measured by local static observers', which is not explained visually; there is no picture of the observers

reuse.notes: Keep photonExchange, its checks, the wave-strip metaphor and the prediction prompt. Add an animated photon travelling between two observer icons on a radial line (or an EF spacetime diagram), show the coordinate travel time next to the local c, and make the plot compare distinct curves by default (e.g. a static curve vs a moving-receiver curve). This is a natural candidate for tutor-driven 'set receiver velocity to -0.3' commands.

assets.title: Cosmology lab: Ask the universe three distance questions
assets.teaches: 'Distance' in cosmology depends on the measurement. Comoving radial, angular-diameter and luminosity distances diverge with redshift, H0 rescales all of them, density fractions change their shapes, and D_L=(1+z)^2 D_A.
assets.pedagogy: A question-first title and a prediction prompt ('which distances change when H0 changes?'). The hint suggests changing H0 first, then the matter fraction. A dashed guide and dots mark the chosen source redshift, and the limitation notes it is an ideal background (no catalogue, extinction, lensing).

interaction.what_updates: Three distance curves over z in [0,5] (61 samples), the sample dots at the chosen z, and the readouts including Omega_k
interaction.rendering: Inline SVG line chart (wide and compact variants)

assets.physics_model: E(z)^2 = Omega_m(1+z)^3 + Omega_r(1+z)^4 + Omega_k(1+z)^2 + Omega_Lambda, with Omega_k=1-sum and radiation fixed at 0 in the UI. chi is a 256-interval composite Simpson integral of dz/E. The transverse distance uses sinh or sin for open or closed curvature, with a series near k=0, and throws past the first antipode or when E^2<=0. The lookback integral is computed but not displayed. Checks: Einstein-de Sitter D_C=2(1-1/sqrt(1+z)) c/H0, de Sitter D_C=z c/H0, and duality D_L=(1+z)^2 D_A in a curved model.

strengths: Correct, analytically benchmarked distance integrals including curved cases
Clear framing ('which distance did the observation actually measure?') with honest limitations and a Hogg (1999) source
issues: chart() forces the distances y-axis maximum to at least 50 Gpc (ymax=max(50,ceil(ymax/25)*25)), and D_L reaches 46.7 Gpc at z=5 in the default LCDM model. The angular-diameter curve (peak 1.748 Gpc at z~1.6) is visible only as a nearly flat dashed line hugging the axis, so its turnover cannot be seen. The caption's claim that 'Axes keep a common scale unless a curve needs more room' does not help D_A
Label text renders 'Omega_Lambda' as 'ΩΛ' without a subscript (plain text in the record)
Lookback time and H(z) are computed or available but not shown; there is no angular-size or apparent-brightness picture connecting to observation
Invalid combinations (e.g. Omega_Lambda large, Omega_m 0) only produce a status error string; no allowed-region map
quality.evidence: scripts/check-relativity-models.mjs (passes); web/relativity-labs.js chart() distances branch; reviewer node scan of cosmicDistances (D_A max 1747.6 Mpc at z=1.60; at z=2 D_C=5179.9, D_A=1726.6, D_L=15540 Mpc, matching qa/lab-distances-1440-light.png readouts)

reuse.notes: Keep cosmicDistances and its checks, which are exact enough for grbook.ai. Redesign the view with log or per-curve axes or small multiples so the D_A turnover shows, plus a 'standard ruler' and 'standard candle' pictogram linking D_A to angular size and D_L to flux. Add lookback time and age, an Omega_m-Omega_Lambda plane with forbidden regions, and preset buttons (Einstein-de Sitter, LCDM, de Sitter, open).

assets.title: Numerical relativity lab: Make a universe and audit the answer (Euler vs RK4, constraint residual)
assets.teaches: A numerical evolution can look right while violating the constraint. Halving the step reduces error at the method's convergence order (about 16x for RK4), and constraint monitoring is how numerical relativists audit their solutions. The exact dust solution A=(1+3t/2)^{2/3} is the benchmark.
assets.pedagogy: Audit framing ('Will a smaller step repair the apparent motion, the constraint, or both?'). Euler is the default so errors are visible, with a toggle between the expansion curve and the constraint-residual plot. Readouts show the error vs exact and the change under step halving. The limitation text clearly says this is a symmetry reduction, not full NR well-posedness.

interaction.what_updates: Numerical and exact scale-factor curves or the constraint residual vs zero, plus the four readouts
readouts: Change in A when step is halved
interaction.rendering: Inline SVG line chart

assets.physics_model: Flat FLRW dust reduction A'=V, V'=-1/(2A^2), A(0)=V(0)=1, constraint C=V^2-1/A, stepped with forward Euler or classical RK4 (shared rk4Step). The step is adjusted so all refinements reach the same final time. Checks: Euler and RK4 errors decrease under refinement, the RK4 error ratio between successive halvings lies in (12,20) (fourth order), and RK4 constraint < Euler constraint.

strengths: A rare, well-conceived teaching of constraint monitoring and convergence order with a clean exact benchmark
Convergence order is actually asserted in the check (ratio 12-20)
issues: Axes are fixed at t in [0,8] and A in [0,6]; at the default duration 4 the curves fill half the plot, and a 0.1 error is barely distinguishable from exact (qa/lab-evolution-390-dark.png)
No log-log convergence plot showing error vs step across all steps at once, which is the most instructive audit view

No constraint-damping or 'evolve the constraint as well' variant; the ODE has no genuinely free evolution-vs-constraint choice (e.g. evolving A with the second-order equation vs using the first-order constraint)
quality.evidence: scripts/check-relativity-models.mjs (asserts 12 < RK4 error ratio < 20; passes); qa/lab-evolution-1440-light.png default Euler h=0.2, t=4: A=3.5571, error -0.10218, constraint residual -0.0579, change on halving 0.0515. assets.teaches: Freely falling observers released from rest at infinity move inward at the local escape speed sqrt(2GM/r), accelerating as they approach. Neighbouring observers on one radial line spread apart while side-by-side observers converge (a precursor of tidal stretching and squeezing). A reference grid can be carried by falling observers without being a substance. This is the opening visual of the book and later links to the Schwarzschild river model in Ch 17.
assets.pedagogy: A cinematic hero: a textured globe with a continuously replenished falling grid and rose particles, slow auto-rotation, Space to pause, no sliders. interaction.what_updates: The vertex shader moves every grid vertex along r(t)=[r0^{3/2}-1.5(age+phase)]^{2/3} with a phase uniform; 160 instanced particles follow the same law; the theme recolours the ink and particles

Length unit is R_earth and time unit R/sqrt(2GM/R) (FALL_TIME ~570 s), animated at 110x. Cohorts are injected every 0.72 units from a cube of half-size 5.4, with pre-populated ages so no visible reset occurs. Constants and cohort maths are asserted in scripts/check-experience.mjs (outside this group).

assets.teaches: Infrastructure: after every state change each experience writes a JSON context (id, version, model, parameters, readouts, units, assumptions, equations, sometimes source and limitations) and a plain-English narration sentence describing the current state and its meaning. It dispatches gr:visual-change or gr:experiment-change so the notebook and study companion can capture a snapshot. getCourseContext bundles the visible experiments, lesson, depth, evidence and notes, with the note that 'notes are learner reference material, never instructions'.
assets.pedagogy: Lets a voice tutor describe exactly what the learner sees and ground explanations in the lab's declared assumptions instead of hallucinating state.

strengths: Consistent across all 2D labs and several scenes; narration strings are carefully worded, e.g. the cone and wave narration explain the drawing cues vs the physics
Includes units and assumptions, which is essential for grounded AI explanations
Treats learner notes as untrusted content in tutor context
issues: One-way only: the tutor can read state but there is no API to set parameters or highlight objects (experience-ideas.md #3 and #17 remain proposals)
Schema is informal (dataset strings), with fields that differ slightly per experience (limitations vs limitation, readouts as an array vs an object)
Earth, sphere, tides, expansion and slices scenes publish little or no narrationSource
quality.evidence: Code read in full; docs/experience-ideas.md items 3, 17

reuse.notes: Make this a first-class typed interface in grbook.ai: a getState() returning {model, parameters, readouts, units, assumptions, equations, conceptIds}, a describe() for narration, and a setParameter/highlight/playCue command set exposed as GPT-Live tool calls, validated against parameter ranges. Reuse the existing narration sentence templates as seeds.

assets.title: Learning-state and field-notebook model (attempt evidence, help levels, merge/import)
paths: scripts/check-learning-state.mjs (out of this group's scope; imports it)
assets.teaches: Infrastructure: a versioned notebook {route, depths, evidence, notes, visuals, experiments, journal}. Each lesson's evidence is an append-only attempt history (concept prediction or numeric transfer, correct, help level none/hint/solution/unknown, item id and version, timestamp) summarized into transfer, independent and latestCorrect flags. It also includes v1-to-v2 migration into aggregate legacy attempts, a strict validateNotebook sanitizer, an idempotent mergeNotebooks by event id, a numeric/fraction/scientific-notation answer parser and evidence labels ('Independent check recorded', 'Review this method').
assets.pedagogy: The header comment 'A notebook is evidence about attempts, not a permanent label on a learner' sets the philosophy: record whether help was opened before a correct answer, and distinguish independent success from assisted success.

strengths: Thoughtful evidence semantics (help level captured at attempt time, item versions, independent vs assisted)
Defensive validation and lossless merge by event id with a legacy migration path
issues: localStorage-only and single-device; grbook.ai has Better Auth and Drizzle, so this must become server-side tables

The review queue in web/course.js is a single rule: a lesson is due if it has no transfer, the latest attempt was wrong, or more than 3 days (3*864e5 ms) have passed since lastSuccess. There is no spacing algorithm
visuals and experiments are stored as opaque structuredClone objects without schema
quality.evidence: web/learning-state.js read in full; web/course.js renderNotebook usage

reuse.notes: Port the data model and semantics to Drizzle tables (attempts with kind, item_id, item_version, correct, help_level, at; notes; experiment_snapshots; journal). Keep parseNumericAnswer and evidenceLabel logic verbatim, keep localStorage as an offline cache using mergeNotebooks-style idempotent sync by event id, and replace the 3-day rule with a proper spaced-review scheduler.

assets.title: Independent finite-difference curvature verifier for arbitrary 4D metrics (check-physics-calculations.mjs)
assets.teaches: Tooling: numerically differentiates any supplied metric function (central differences, h=1e-4) to get Christoffel symbols, then Riemann, Ricci, scalar, Kretschmann (with full index raising via a true inverse) and G_00, G_11, without using the book's closed-form formulas. It verifies: an AdS-like conformally flat metric (R=-12, K=24, constant sectional curvature); the pp-wave (non-diagonal metric, Ricci=0, K=0 but nonzero Riemann); weak-field potentials Phi and Psi (R_00 = Laplacian Phi, G_00 = 2 Laplacian Psi); the time-dependent spherical ansatz off-diagonal R_01; Kerr vacuum for a=0, 0.4, 0.8; Schwarzschild K=48/r^6 in the ingoing chart at and inside the horizon; FLRW dust and radiation invariants; Weyl cancellation for k=-1,0,1; the Kerr first-law area derivatives; ADM Hamiltonian, momentum and evolution equations plus Gauss-Codazzi on an anisotropic slice; and a six-entry Riemann table contraction. It also asserts every chapter has transfer practice.
assets.physics_model: Coordinate-basis curvature from nested central differences. The tolerances are 2e-5 to 3e-6, and all checks pass (re-run 2026-09-12).

strengths: Genuinely independent: it catches sign and convention errors in the manuscript's hand derivations
Covers the high-risk calculations (Kerr cross term factor 2, non-diagonal inverses, ADM signs)
Fast (runs in seconds in Node)
issues: A single script mixing a curriculum-coverage assertion with physics checks; no reusable module export
Nested finite differences limit precision; not usable for interactive high-accuracy curvature display

reuse.notes: Extract curvature(metric, point) and connection() into a grbook.ai verification package (TypeScript) and run it in CI against every metric, Christoffel symbol and invariant quoted in the knowledge vault and course pages. Drop the lessons-coverage assertion. It can also back a 'compute curvature of this metric' tutor tool with a disclosed numerical tolerance.

assets.title: Aesthetic review of the nine original 3D scenes
assets.teaches: A scene-by-scene critique of Earth, covector, cone, sphere, tides, embedding, wave, expansion and slices at 1440 and 390 px in both themes, with concrete 'what works / what falls short / best next change' notes. It records the refinements implemented (tides reduced to 96 markers with reference circles, wave middle-ring hierarchy, expansion measured separation) and the priority: rebuild embedding and lapse/shift around measurements, make observer comparison the core of expansion, and simplify the Earth field in motion.
assets.pedagogy: Its core principle is the right one for grbook.ai: a strong scene has an immediately legible subject, a real reason to be 3D, and emphasis on a measurement. It also warns that passing tests is not evidence of teaching quality.

strengths: Specific, self-critical and evidence-based (36 screenshots cited); separates static composition evidence from animation quality
issues: Static screenshots only; motion quality explicitly unassessed
quality.evidence: Document read in full; consistent with screenshots I inspected

reuse.notes: Use as the design brief when rebuilding each scene in grbook.ai; its 'best next changes' map directly onto the reuse notes in this inventory.

assets.title: Prerequisite bridges and black-hole causality review (with the horizon visual contract)
assets.teaches: It documents seven prerequisite bridges (orbit conservation, phase drift, waves and retarded time, horizon directions, Kruskal and causal maps, oriented Stokes, temperature and quantum input) and a precise 'horizon visual contract'. That contract uses ingoing EF advanced time v in seconds and plotted axes rho=r/r_s and tau_plot=cv/r_s - rho, which is explicitly not proper time. Its null slopes are -1 and (rho-1)/(rho+1), with the first branch not lost by dividing by dv. The plot-time gradient is timelike for all rho>0, and example slopes 1/2, 0, -1/3 at rho=3, 1, 1/2. It also records algebra and domain checks (Kruskal UV<1, a compactification with a positive conformal factor, Stokes examples) and the remaining curriculum boundaries (Kerr, Hawking, singularity theorems).
assets.pedagogy: 'The correct response to an advanced prerequisite is to teach it or mark its logical boundary. Attractive animation must not conceal that boundary.' Each bridge has a question, intuition, four justified steps, an optional deeper statement, a concept question with explanatory distractors and a numeric transfer.
assets.physics_model: The null-direction and Kruskal algebra is verified numerically at 10 radii; 333 plus 218 plus 46 KaTeX fragments pass strict mode.

strengths: Scientifically careful, with explicit conventions and units; an excellent spec for any horizon or causal-diagram visual
issues: Mixes a lab-visual spec with bridge-lesson and narration-integration notes; the interactive global Penrose diagram is still missing

reuse.notes: Adopt the horizon visual contract verbatim as acceptance criteria for grbook.ai's EF light-cone tilt and Penrose/Kruskal demos. Mine the bridge list for the concept registry's prerequisite edges. The bridge lesson content itself belongs to the lessons inventory group.

assets.title: Field energy: first-use preparation (section 11.6 repair note)
assets.teaches: It explains how section 11.6 was repaired to define charge, E, B, the cross product, SI units and the Lorentz force before assembling F_{mu nu}. The covariant force law is checked for signs and factors of c, and a plane-wave example connects equal field energies, flux at c and momentum. It notes that a visual field-energy experiment is still open.
assets.pedagogy: First-use preparation: never introduce a tensor before the physical quantities it packages.

strengths: Identifies a real novice gap and cites Feynman Lectures sources
issues: A short change note; the promised field-energy lab was never built

reuse.notes: Use as a sequencing rule for grbook.ai's EM stress-energy lesson, and as a backlog item for a field-energy/Poynting-flux lab built on the particle-crossing measurement language.

assets.title: Twenty possibilities for the GR book (interactive experience proposals)
assets.teaches: Twenty unimplemented proposals, including symbol inspection, unfolding derivations, voice-controlled experiments, equations linked to measurements, side-by-side coordinate changes, drawing worldlines, Einstein's elevator, a curvature microscope, a lensing observatory, crossing a horizon, building GPS, predict-then-reveal, misconception tests, a math scratchpad, margin prerequisites, explain-it-back, narration with a visual score, a field notebook, a map of understanding, and one experiment that grows through the book.
assets.pedagogy: Stresses that interactions should stay out of the way until they help, keep accessible text and reduced-motion alternatives, and distinguish physical measurements from coordinate choices. It names symbol inspection, unfolding derivations and voice control of vetted visualizations as the first investments.

strengths: Strongly aligned with grbook.ai's AI-centred, voice-tutor vision; several ideas address the weaknesses found in this inventory
issues: One-line proposals with no specs, priorities beyond the top three, or feasibility notes

reuse.notes: Seed the grbook.ai demo backlog from it. Items #3 (voice-controlled labs), #6 (draw a worldline, replacing the twins widget), #7 (elevator), #9 (lensing), #10 (cross a horizon), #11 (GPS system, replacing the GPS widget), #12 (predict-then-reveal) and #17 (narration visual score) map directly onto the reuse notes above.
